subject.title: Feature: Tool-level sandbox mode for selective isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-tool execution-placement contract, and if so should placement be operator-configured, tool/plugin-declared, or a precedence-controlled combination?
rationale: This changes sandbox isolation and host escape semantics for untrusted-content tools, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary or config schema without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Core Placement Contract
options.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, tool filtering, browser behavior, web_fetch behavior, gateway-owned tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

options.title: Keep Current Model
options.body: Reject per-tool placement for now and document the intended model as session sandboxing plus elevated exec and sandbox tool policy filtering.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Sandbox Program
options.body: Make a broader sandbox/security issue the canonical design home and use this issue only as evidence for the per-tool placement use case.

recommendation.title: Design Core Placement Contract
recommendation.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, tool filtering, browser behavior, web_fetch behavior, gateway-owned tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed the issue as open product/security work and has recent path history on the sandbox runtime/docs boundary.
